title: S9 - Booking core
description: Weeks 17-18. Exit: a Scheduler role exists in both apps, patients can use the whole app on the web except the camera, patients can request sessions on web and Android, and a Scheduler can confirm or refuse them without double-booking.
goal: Let patients request in-center sessions and let a Scheduler decide them safely.
entry_criteria: Confirm owners and realistic capacity before starting.
Required predecessor deliverables are available or scheduled in dependency order.

exit_criteria.description: All sprint issues meet their acceptance criteria and completion evidence requirements.

Grant the Scheduler role, request a session as a patient on the web and on Android, then confirm one request and reject another in the Scheduler table, showing two simultaneous requests for the last place cannot both succeed.

demo: Grant the Scheduler role, request a session as a patient on the web and on Android, then confirm one request and reject another in the Scheduler table, showing two simultaneous requests for the last place cannot both succeed.
risks: Adding a role touches sign-in on Android, so the parser must change before any account holds the new role.
A pending request holds capacity, so a cap per patient is required to stop one account filling the calendar.
Patient pages reuse staff views, and row-level security alone would show an administrator everyone's records.

execution_plan.first_week: Work prerequisites first; review integration and design risks midweek.
execution_plan.second_week: Integrate, execute acceptance checks, fix defects and demonstrate the sprint outcome.
execution_plan.capacity_policy: Estimates are provisional; reserve approximately 20% of actual team capacity for integration and defects.

issues.description: Create a Scheduler role that only an Admin can assign, using the same mechanism as the Therapist role, limited to scheduling and kept away from clinical data.

acceptance_criteria.description: Only an active administrator can grant or revoke the Scheduler role, and not on their own account, through admin_set_role.
Both administrator apps offer the role in account details, a Schedulers filter and a Schedulers count, and both call the same functions. check_admin_parity.py passes and ADMIN-PARITY.md is updated.
Android signs in an account holding scheduler or any unknown role without failing, and a Scheduler gets their own tabs rather than the patient ones.
The web routes a Scheduler to /scheduler, in the order Admin, Scheduler, Therapist, Patient, matching Android.

A signed-in non-Scheduler gets a 403 page at /scheduler and HTTP 403 from scheduler functions. A generic test finds every scheduler_ function and proves this for each role, so later functions are covered automatically.
A Scheduler reads no other person's sessions, measurements, prescriptions, assignments, consents or patient profiles, proved by tests.
A Scheduler on Android sees the note that scheduling is on the web, confirmed in the real app on an emulator.

issues.title: Model center hours, holidays, closures and availability
issues.description: Give the database one source of truth for when the center can see patients, and a function that lists specific bookable times.

functions.name: booking_availability
functions.description: Return working days and their specific time slots for a date range, in the center time zone, with places remaining.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.name: slot_problem
functions.description: Explain why a time cannot be booked. Shared by requests, confirmation and rescheduling.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

acceptance_criteria.description: Migrations create center_settings, center_hours, center_holidays and center_closures, seeded with 60-minute slots, capacity 3, 24-hour cut-offs and Monday to Friday 09:00-17:00.
Every holiday in Proclamation 1006 (2026) and Proclamation 1427 (2027) is seeded. February 25, a special working day, is not, so it stays bookable.
booking_availability returns specific slots with a start and end time and places remaining, and hides past times, times inside the minimum notice and times beyond the booking horizon.
Weekends when closed, national holidays, seasonal holidays and closures are not bookable. A time-range closure removes only the slots it overlaps. Tests cover each case.
Times are stored in UTC and slot boundaries are correct in Asia/Manila whatever the client's time zone.
Clients cannot write these tables directly, and closure reasons are visible to Schedulers only.

functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.name: record_booking_event

functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

acceptance_criteria.description: bookings has a unique reference number, the statuses pending, confirmed, rejected, cancelled and rescheduled, and specific start and end times. Clients have no direct writes.
Database exclusion constraints reject overlapping active bookings for one patient and for one therapist, even for a direct insert that bypasses the functions.
Parallel requests for the last place in a slot: exactly the capacity succeed, proved by a concurrent test against real PostgREST.
request_booking refuses holidays, closures, past times, times inside the minimum notice, full slots and accounts over the active-booking cap. A repeated client ID returns the original booking.
scheduler_confirm requires a therapist and re-validates hours, holidays, closures, capacity and therapist conflicts at the moment of confirmation.
Reject and cancel require a reason. Reschedule requires a specific slot and a therapist. Bulk reject applies to pending requests only.
A patient can cancel only their own pending or confirmed booking, and only before the cut-off.

Every status change writes who, what and when to an immutable booking_events row through a trigger, mirrored to audit_events. Both administrator activity feeds show it under a Bookings category, with the same wording.
Revoking the therapist role or disabling a therapist returns their future bookings to Pending without a therapist.

issues.title: Give patients the whole app on the web, except the camera
issues.description: Replace the "use the mobile app" page with a full patient workspace. Everything a patient can do on Android works on the web, and only the camera exercise suggests the phone.
issues.requirements: Booking brief, section 6; owner clarification 2026-11-06: patients can use the web, and only the camera feature is unavailable there

acceptance_criteria.description: A patient who signs in on the web lands on /patient, and the old /use-mobile page is gone. Staff who also hold the patient role can switch to it.

Home shows the next exercise, this week and recent sessions. Exercises lists assignments with targets and instructions. Progress shows history, filters and charts. All filter to the signed-in account.
Profile covers details, photo, password and language, plus consent status and withdrawal, export and deletion requests with their status, and joining a therapist by code.

Starting an exercise or the camera check shows the suggestion to use the phone, with a store link or QR code when VITE_ANDROID_APP_URL is set. A browser test proves the exercise does not run and the page never requests the camera.
The workspace works at phone width with no sideways scrolling, by keyboard, and passes axe.
After a consent withdrawal on the web, Android reads the server's latest consent on refresh and records a new grant before the next session, proved by a unit test.
docs/PLAN.md and WEB-DESIGN.md no longer say patients stay on Android, and every new string exists in English and Filipino.
